title: A Gigantic Molecular Wheel of {Gd140}: A New Member of the Molecular Wheel Family

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.formula: [Gd140(CO3)20(μ3-OH)100(CH3COO)80(LH3)40(H2O)200](NO3)80·(H2O)x (x approximately 80; LH3 is triply deprotonated myo-inositol)

synthesis.procedure: The main text describes hydrolysis of a gadolinium(III) salt in the presence of acetate and myo-inositol, with carbonate generated by absorption of atmospheric CO2. It mentions reflux but gives no reagent quantities or complete preparation. The text names Gd(ClO4)3 in one passage and Gd(NO3)3·6H2O in another; the starting salt cannot be resolved from the supplied main text.

reagents.name: gadolinium(III) salt (identity inconsistent in main text)
sodium hydroxide solution
reagents.amount: 1.0 M aqueous solution; added dropwise until incipient permanent precipitation

synthesis.time: 2 hours under reflux; crystals formed after about one month
synthesis.vessel_or_method: hydrolysis under reflux with atmospheric CO2 absorption
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered while hot; the filtrate was evaporated in a beaker under ambient conditions to afford block-shaped colorless crystals.

properties.summary: Magnetic measurements and fitting indicate weak antiferromagnetic interactions. The cluster exhibits a measured magnetocaloric effect.

measurements.conditions: 300 K; temperature-dependence plot measured under a 1000 Oe dc field

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A discrete, approximately 6.0 nm outer-diameter wheel with tenfold symmetry, assembled from ten saddle-like {Gd14} subunits. Each subunit contains a carbonate- and hydroxide-bridged Gd14 core stabilized by acetate, deprotonated myo-inositol, and aqua ligands. Adjacent subunits alternate in orientation and are joined through hydroxide and myo-inositol oxygen bridges. The wheel has an approximately 3.4 nm inner diameter.
